clue.text: Piece of sacking very small person gets to sew

indicators.note: a piece is only a small part, so just one letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: a titch is British slang for a tiny person

explanation.surface: A tiny tailor is handed a scrap of sacking and told to get sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: TITCH is informal British for a very small person.
explanation.definitionFit: To stitch is to sew, joining fabric with a needle and thread.

clue.text: Cabinet ministers ultimately chose a leader of wisdom, possibly

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the closing letter of ministers is used
possibly suggests one arrangement among many, so the letters may be reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of wisdom is used

explanation.surface: Cabinet ministers end up picking a wise figure as their leader, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' reads as the government body, but it is the piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a glass-fronted display cabinet for exhibiting objects.

clue.text: Crime fighters in Nile port, all over the place

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Police are chasing criminals in chaotic scenes at an Egyptian river port.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation that coordinates efforts against crime across borders.

clue.text: Musical, presumably in black and white!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stage show by Tim Rice with Benny and Björn of ABBA
second meaning: a board game played with black and white pieces on black and white squares

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an old monochrome film musical; 'presumably' flags the playful second reading of the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is both a 1980s stage musical and a game whose board and pieces come in two colours.

clue.text: US artist left with monarch after game

indicators.note: after places the first pieces behind the game word, which therefore leads

explanation.surface: An American painter departs, accompanied by a king or queen, once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill Whistler was an American-born painter, famous for the portrait of his mother.

clue.text: Country singer, Kim, was in hall, playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are being toyed with and moved around

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A country singer called Kim was performing in a concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Hank Williams was a hugely influential American country music singer-songwriter of the 1940s and 50s.

clue.text: Fabric in his cot, all frilly

indicators.note: frilly means ruffled and gathered, so the letters are ruffled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The material in the baby's cot is all frills.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailcloth is a strong canvas fabric used for making sails and sometimes clothing.

clue.text: Convict with nothing on in small lake

parts.note: an old lag is a seasoned convict

explanation.surface: A naked prisoner is spotted bathing in a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG, as in 'old lag', is British slang for a prisoner; 'with nothing on' suggests nudity but is just O and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of shallow water, often cut off from the sea, effectively a small lake.

clue.text: Night flight for cheap whisky

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an overnight plane journey that leaves passengers bleary
second meaning: American slang for rough, inferior whiskey

explanation.surface: Someone takes an overnight flight, attracted by duty-free bargain spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-eye is both an overnight flight arriving early morning and US slang for raw, low-grade whiskey.

clue.text: Unfashionable group coming from launch

parts.note: a set is a group or clique

explanation.surface: A dowdy band of people emerges from a product launch.
explanation.definitionFit: The outset is the start of something, as is its launch.

clue.text: Crazy to remove a door, say, with bit of draught ensuing

indicators.note: ensuing means following on, so this piece comes after the first

parts.note: taking a door off its hinges; 'say' marks the door as one example

indicators.note: a bit is only a small part, so a single letter is taken from the next word

explanation.surface: It is mad to take a door off its hinges and let a cold draught in.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhinged is an idiom for mentally unbalanced, as if the mind had come off its hinges.

clue.text: Annoyed department obtaining random sample

explanation.surface: An irritated office department carries out a random survey.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-section is a sample taken to represent the whole of a population.

clue.text: Treacherous rocks ahead of rowers? This might help one who gets in the drink

definitions.text: This might help one who gets in the drink

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first piece in front of the second
treacherous suggests something twisted and unreliable, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Rowers face dangerous rocks; something might rescue a person who falls into the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the drink' suggests falling overboard, but it means getting into a bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the tool that pulls a cork, letting a drinker get at the wine.

clue.text: Friend — shed tears about one out East

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the weeping word wraps round the rest
out means removed, so the compass point that follows is dropped from the number word

explanation.surface: A pal weeps over someone who has gone away to the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One out East' reads as a person travelling, but it means the number word losing its compass letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crony is a close friend or companion, often with a hint of cliquishness.

clue.text: A monk's seldom prepared a fish dish

indicators.note: prepared as in cooked up, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A monk rarely cooks a fish course for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoked salmon is cured fish served as a dish, typically a starter.

clue.text: Put out the Spanish one, at home in match

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the word for a contest

parts.note: to match is to pair or mate
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: A Spanish player, playing at home, is knocked out in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate a competitor is to put them out of a contest.

clue.text: Refuse to entertain ICI executive

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one word holds the other

explanation.surface: A boss turns down an invitation to wine and dine the chemicals company ICI.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish. ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a big British company.
explanation.definitionFit: An official is a person holding an executive position in an organisation.

clue.text: Exclamation from popular singer dropping ring

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A pop star cries out when a ring slips from his finger.
explanation.walkthrough: Boy George was the lead singer of Culture Club.
explanation.definitionFit: 'By George!' is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise.

clue.text: Spy MiG flight out of control? That's highly unlikely

indicators.note: something out of control tumbles in disorder, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy plane spirals out of control; surely that could never happen.
explanation.walkthrough: A MiG is a Russian fighter jet.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a sarcastic retort meaning something will never happen.

clue.text: NW town featured in first half of book

indicators.note: only the first half survives, so the back half of the word is cut away

parts.note: a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A northern town gets a mention early in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The book is the Bible's Ecclesiastes, twelve letters, so its first six are kept. Eccles is a town near Manchester, famous for Eccles cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccles is a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England.

clue.text: Ceremony in outskirts of Windsor for author

indicators.note: in places the ceremony inside the edge letters
outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters of the place name are taken

parts.note: the first and last letters of Windsor

explanation.surface: A ceremony on the edge of Windsor is held in honour of an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer is an author of books or articles.

clue.text: Dog found in cul-de-sac or ginnel

indicators.note: found in says the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of sac, all of or, and the start of ginnel

explanation.surface: A dog turns up in a dead-end street or narrow alley.
explanation.walkthrough: A ginnel is a northern English word for a narrow passage between houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by the Queen.

clue.text: Bell tower seen from tents pitched by a river

parts.note: a camp is where tents are pitched

explanation.surface: Campers by a river can see a bell tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanile is a freestanding bell tower, especially an Italian one.

clue.text: Collect a large amount

parts.note: a mass of something is a lot of it

explanation.surface: Gather a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction, but 'Collect' is the definition and the rest builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a large quantity.

clue.text: Gay seducer unwilling to visit a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A cheerful womaniser is reluctant to travel to a Brazilian harbour city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is used in its old sense of carefree and light-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a rakish man who seduces women, from a character in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: Artist on platform showing off sword

parts.note: a pier is a platform jutting into water

explanation.surface: A performer on stage shows off with a sword.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed sword used for thrusting.

clue.text: Rank of Frenchman, social worker?

parts.note: ants are social insects that work

explanation.surface: Someone asks the job title of a Frenchman employed in social services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' sounds like a care professional, but it is an ant, a social insect famous for toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergeant is a non-commissioned military or police rank.

clue.text: Legendary lover is elderly head of empire

indicators.note: the head is the top, so just the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A storied romantic is now an aged ruler of an empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess in the medieval legend of Tristan and Isolde, a tale of doomed love.
